newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa sees Dm 100mln passenger savings.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees Dm 100mln passenger savings.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it aims to save up to 100 million marks in travel distribution costs through cutting travel agents' commissions.
Lufthansa passenger sales chief executive Hemjo Klein told a news conference the airline would introduce a restructured commissions system on May 1, 1997.
The airline aimed to reduce external sales distribution costs, mostly travel agents' commissions, by up to 100 million marks, he said.
But Klein admitted last-minute concessions in negotiations with travel agents' associations would reduce the airline's planned savings by "several million marks".
Lufthansa dropped a 500,000 mark minimum turnover figure for eligibility for bonus payments and did not include its five percent 1997 capacity rise in sales calculations, he said.
The new structure was negotiated in four rounds of talks with travel agent associations DRV and ASR which ended at Monday midday and was unveiled at a joint news conference.
Under the new-look system, Lufthansa will reduce commissions for sales of inner-German tickets to five percent from nine percent but retain commissions on international ticket sales at nine percent.
Klein said some two billion marks out of total Germany sales revenue of 6.7 billion marks was generated by domestic flights.
Germany sales manager Stefan Pichler said performance-related bonus commissions would be paid to all agents on additional sales volume, to selected destinations and for electronic ticket sales.
Klein added that Lufthansa would reach separate commissions deals soon with major travel agency chains but these were based on the same revised commissions system.
These travel agency chains had a 70 percent share of Lufthansa's inner-German sales and an overall 52 percent share of its Germany sales revenue, he noted.
These included Hapag-Lloyd AG, Deutsches Reisebuero GmbH and American Express Co, Pichler told Reuters.
